reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Joint county bridge construction and subdivision contributions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8539). Covers permissive uniting of county commissions to build a necessary bridge across a county-dividing watercourse with agreed expense proportions, plus permissive cost contributions by other counties, municipalities, townships, road districts, or road-jurisdiction subdivisions deeming the bridge a benefit.

headings.title: Bridge plans, contracts, and construction supervision
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers preparation of plans and specifications, contract letting, and construction supervision by the uniting counties' county highway engineers, either of them, or otherwise as agreed by the county commissions.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8539) and verified all fingerprints. Checked permissive uniting of counties over a county-line watercourse on agreed cost proportions, permissive contributions from other counties/municipalities/townships/road districts/subdivisions, and county highway engineer or agreed plans, contracting, and supervision; both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: State-line bridge cooperation and shared costs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1, history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8541, A.L. 1945 p. 1481), and cross-reference (227.080). Covers permissive cooperation between bordering Missouri county commissions and an adjoining state or its county authorities to build bridge(s) over a state-line watercourse on agreed cost proportions. Independent review revised title from 'Interstate county cooperation and shared bridge costs' because Missouri counties may unite with an adjoining state itself as well as adjoining-state county authorities.

headings.title: Supervision, private subscriptions, and petitioned township tax levy
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and section notes. Covers agreed competent supervision of plans, contracting, and construction; permissive receipt of private subscriptions by Missouri county commissions; and mandatory county commission levy of the full special road and bridge tax under Mo. Const. Art. X, § 12 (first sentence, first paragraph) upon petition of a majority of taxpaying township citizens to build or create a perpetuated bridge-building fund.

headings.title: Appropriations from county road and bridge fund
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and section notes. Covers permissive county commission appropriations from the county road and bridge fund to pay all or part of building state-line bridges.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all three subsections, history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8541, A.L. 1945 p. 1481), and cross-reference (227.080), and verified all fingerprints. Checked Missouri county cooperation with an adjoining state or its county authorities, agreed competent supervision, private subscriptions, petitioned township special road and bridge tax under Mo. Const. Art. X, § 12, and county road and bridge fund appropriations. Revised subsection 1 to 'State-line bridge cooperation and shared costs'; retained subsections 2-3.

headings.title: Eligibility, landowner petitions, and appointing three commissioners
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8555 through A.L. 1990 H.B. 1621). Covers eligibility triggers (city of 200,000+ proposing to pay at least half of reasonable right-of-way cost with county debt-limit/bond-vote obstacle, or petition by owners of a majority of county acres within two miles of bridge/site), conclusive commission finding on petition signatures, appointment of three resident landowner commissioners, and replacement of non-qualifying or non-performing appointees.

headings.title: Commissioner qualification and oath filing deadline
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers 10-day deadline after appointment for commissioners to take, subscribe, and file with the county clerk the constitutional oath and oath of faithful, honest, and impartial performance.

headings.title: Mapping, land valuations, and distance-zone classification
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers commissioners preparing a map and land list within 10 miles of the bridge on the county's side of the stream, fixing fair valuations independent of buildings, assigning tracts into four distance zones (up to 2, >2 to 4, >4 to 7, >7 to 10 miles) under the major-portion rule, and identifying multicounty locations.

headings.title: Meaning of lands in this section
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Defines "lands" for section 234.120 to mean both lands and lots regardless of whether located inside an incorporated city, town, or village.

headings.title: Valuation tie-breaking, list filing, and published hearing notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Covers averaging commissioners' separate valuations when they disagree, certifying and filing the land list with the county clerk, and publishing weekly newspaper notice (at least two insertions) in each affected county setting boundaries, assessment liability, and a hearing date at least two weeks after first publication for written objections.

headings.title: Objection hearings, list approval, purchase contracts, and bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Covers rescheduling notice if not in session, written objections and evidentiary hearings/continuances, commission alterations, approval, and certification of the list, allowing commissioner pay (up to $5/day) and engineer/attorney expenses, contracting with the city to purchase the right-of-way, and issuing special assessment bonds covering county share, expenses, discount, and initial interest.

headings.title: Bond denominations, interest dates, installments, and payment place
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Covers minimum $100 denominations, lawful interest payable April 1 and October 1, annual principal installments (not required to be equal) maturing within 20 years with the last at least 18 years after bond date, and payment at a named bank or trust company.

headings.title: Bond execution, state auditor registration, and treasurer custody
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and history note. Covers execution by the presiding commissioner and attestation/registration by the county clerk, state auditor registration applying section 108.260 as amended, and county treasurer custody until disposition.

headings.title: Bond sale floor and limited payment sources
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and history note. Covers permissive public/private sale or direct right-of-way payment at not less than 95% of face value, and limiting bond/interest payment strictly to special assessments, bond proceeds, and depository interest thereon.

headings.title: Circuit court proceedings to adjudicate bond validity
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 10 and history note. Covers permissive county commission petition (before or after issuance) for circuit court validity adjudication, four successive weekly newspaper notices in each affected county, hearing at the first term 15+ days after last publication, and adjudication of bond validity and assessment liability unless the contrary is proven.

headings.title: Tiered assessment valuations by distance from bridge
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 11 and history note. Covers the issuing county clerk's post-issuance assessment valuation list applying 100% (within 2 miles), 75% (>2 to 4 miles), 50% (>4 to 7 miles), and 25% (>7 to 10 miles) weights to commission-approved valuations.

headings.title: Certifying multicounty land lists and assessment rates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 12 and history note. Covers the issuing county clerk supplying land lists and assessment valuations to other affected county clerks and certifying ordered special assessment rates for their tax books.

headings.title: Annual assessments, liens, penalties, collection, and foreclosure
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 13 and history note. Covers annual county commission assessment orders for due principal/interest, tax-book charging, paramount lien status (except state/county/school/road taxes) covering principal, interest, penalties, collection costs, and attorney fees, default rates, tax-style foreclosure suits, and collector receipting.

headings.title: Prima facie assessment bills and county treasurer custody
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 14 and history note. Covers county assessment bills serving as prima facie evidence in lien enforcement suits, county treasurer custody and official-bond liability for bond and assessment funds, collector remittances, county depositary interest, and disbursement.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all 14 subsections and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8555 through A.L. 1990 H.B. 1621) and verified all fingerprints. Checked 200,000+ city/petition eligibility and commissioner appointment, 10-day oaths, 10-mile mapping and four distance zones, section-specific meaning of 'lands', tie-breaking/notice/objection hearings/purchase contracts/bond issuance, bond terms, § 108.260 registration, 95% sale floor and limited payment sources, circuit court validity adjudication, 100/75/50/25% tiered assessment valuations, multicounty certifications, annual assessments/liens/foreclosure, and prima facie bills/treasurer custody; all 14 drafted titles retained.

headings.title: City bond authority, debt limit, and voter approval
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8556, A.L. 1953 p. 666, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1621). Covers permissive city bond issuance for right-of-way purchases and election/issuance expenses, subject to the constitutional debt limit and voter approval by the constitutionally required percentage.

headings.title: Newspaper publication and posting of election notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers at least three weeks' election notice in a city newspaper (using a qualified daily newspaper if one exists, published at least once weekly with last publication within two weeks of election) or posting ten handbills if no newspaper is published in the city.

headings.title: Election conduct, ward voting places, and combined precincts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers conducting the election like other city elections, subject to the requirement of at least two voting places per ward (when more than one ward) and authority to combine precincts using the host precinct's judges and clerks.

headings.title: Concurrent city elections and separate ballots and boxes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers permissive holding of the bond election simultaneously with another general or special city election using the same precincts, judges, clerks, and booths, but requiring separate ballots and ballot boxes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8556 through A.L. 1990 H.B. 1621) and verified all fingerprints. Checked permissive city bond issuance subject to constitutional debt limit and voter percentage, three-week newspaper/handbill notice, two-voting-places-per-ward and combined-precinct rules, and concurrent election authority requiring separate ballots and ballot boxes; all four drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Payment timing and completion condition for proposed bridges
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8557). Covers permissive city and county payment for bridge right-of-way when funded and properly conveyed, subject to the proviso barring payment for right-of-way over a proposed bridge until bridge completion per plans.

headings.title: Shared roadway upkeep and bridge owner maintenance duty
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers proportional city-county sharing (based on purchase price paid) of paving, lighting, and guarding roadway expenses, while assigning permanent structural preservation and maintenance of the bridge to support the roadway to the bridge owner.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8557) and verified all fingerprints. Checked permissive payment upon funding and conveyance with proposed-bridge completion proviso, proportionate city-county sharing of roadway paving/lighting/guarding expenses, and bridge owner's permanent structural maintenance obligation; both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: County and city duty to open access highways
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8558). Covers requiring every participating county commission to open necessary county access highways and every participating city to open necessary city streets or highways for public bridge access.

headings.title: Circuit court condemnation proceedings under chapter 523
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers permissive circuit court condemnation by the county or city when unable to agree on damages with a landowner or when the owner is legally incapable of conveying, conducted with like effect as provided in chapter 523.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history/prior revisions (RSMo 1939 § 8558) and verified all fingerprints. Checked county and city duties to open necessary bridge access highways/streets and permissive circuit court condemnation conducted under chapter 523 when unable to agree or when an owner is legally incapable of conveying; both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Issuance and sale of toll bridge revenue bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (RSMo 1939 § 8548). Covers permissive issuance by section 234.210 public agencies of negotiable toll bridge revenue bonds for acquiring, constructing, owning, operating, improving, extending, and maintaining toll bridges and approaches, and sale to the United States government/agencies or other investors.

headings.title: Bridge tolls, sinking fund, and revenue allocation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers requiring agencies issuing bonds under sections 234.210 to 234.300 to charge reasonable tolls covering maintenance, repair, operation, and loan-amortization sinking fund (for no other purpose) and to fix, collect, segregate, and allocate tolls and revenues for bond payment. Independent review revised title from 'Mandatory bridge tolls, sinking fund, and revenue allocation' to avoid framing a conditional post-bond-issuance toll requirement as an unconditional mandate.

headings.title: Revenue liens, non-taxation limits, and toll termination
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers permissive liens pledging bridge toll revenue by section 234.210 agencies, prohibitions on tax repayment, liens on other agency property, or pledges of agency credit, and terminating tolls once borrowed funds, interest, and charges are repaid.

headings.title: Bond negotiability, interest cap, maturity, and sale terms
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers permissive negotiability, maximum 6% annual interest rate, annual or semiannual maturities, and issuing-authority discretion over time and manner of sale.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read all four subsections and history note (RSMo 1939 § 8548) and verified all fingerprints. Checked section 234.210 public agency bond issuance/sale, conditional post-issuance toll, sinking-fund, and revenue-allocation duties, revenue liens with non-taxation/non-credit-pledge limits and toll termination upon repayment, and negotiability/6% cap/maturity/sale terms. Revised subsection 2 to 'Bridge tolls, sinking fund, and revenue allocation'; retained subsections 1, 3, and 4.

headings.title: Authority and scope of toll bridge refunding bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1941 p. 525 § 5b). Covers issuing negotiable toll bridge revenue refunding bonds to redeem toll bridge revenue or refunding bonds at maturity, upon voluntary surrender, or upon prior call if expressly reserved, covering principal, redemption premium, accrued/accruing interest, and necessary issuance expenses.

headings.title: Refunding bond terms, interest limit, and security
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers governing-authority discretion over refunding bond dates, maturities, payment places, execution, interest rate (up to 6% annually), and denominations, and securing/paying refunding bonds in the same manner as original revenue bonds under sections 234.210 to 234.300.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1941 p. 525 § 5b) and verified all fingerprints. Checked toll bridge revenue refunding bond authorization for maturity, voluntary surrender, or expressly reserved prior call (covering principal, premium, interest, and issuance expenses) and governing-authority discretion over terms up to 6% annual interest with security matching original bonds under sections 234.210 to 234.300; both drafted titles retained.

headings.title: Consensual maturity extensions, call rights, and rate changes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1941 p. 525 § 5d). Covers governing-authority power, with bondholders' consent, to extend maturities, reserve prior call/redemption rights on interest dates, and change interest rates on outstanding bonds issued under sections 234.210 to 234.300 via bond endorsements and interest coupons without varying other terms. Explicitly notes that the archived text references "refunding bonds as provided for in section 234.220" (whereas refunding bonds appear in section 234.260); source cross-reference retained without silent alteration.

headings.title: Filing proceedings with state auditor without re-registration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers mandatory certification of a full transcript of proceedings and documents relating to any maturity extension, redemption reservation, or interest-rate change to the state auditor for filing, while exempting endorsed bonds with attached coupons from re-registration.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read both subsections and history note (L. 1941 p. 525 § 5d) and verified all fingerprints. Checked bondholder-consensual maturity extensions, prior call reservations, and interest-rate changes via endorsements/coupons without varying other terms, confirmed the archived source cross-reference discrepancy citing 'section 234.220' for refunding bonds (which appear in section 234.260) without silent alteration, and checked state auditor transcript filing without re-registration; both drafted titles retained.
